classification.difficultyReason: Construct unit-circle diagrams and interpret reflected coordinates to illustrate two negative-angle identities.

answer.short: The points at $\theta$ and $-\theta$ are reflections in the $x$-axis and have the same $x$-coordinate. Hence $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$.
answer.worked: Reflection in the $x$-axis takes $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ to $P'(\cos\theta,-\sin\theta)$, the point at angle $-\theta$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, which is unchanged, so $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$.

answer.short: The points at $\theta$ and $-\theta$ are reflections in the $x$-axis and have opposite $y$-coordinates. Hence $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
answer.worked: Reflection in the $x$-axis takes $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ to $P'(\cos\theta,-\sin\theta)$, the point at angle $-\theta$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, whose sign reverses, so $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
